George Eastern of Westbury in the County of Washington and State of Rhode Island on Oath saith in addition and explanation of the testimony heretofore given of services per- formed by Capt Joshua Pendleton during the Revolutionary War; that he was knowing to services performed as stated; that this deponent was the Clerk of said Capt Joshua Pendleton's Company, and that he acted as a Commissary and dealt with the rations to the men, which were furnished by the State of Rhode Island; that said Company furnished a Guard by detachments, which were stationed at Watch Hill and to the Eastward on the Narragansett shore, said Guard were furnished by the State with one nine pound Cannon, and two four pound field piece, that during the said before mentioned the Enemy drove on the shore an English schooner prize to a Privation owned in New London which was hauled from Cark to New York loaded with provisions for the British Army the Enemy boarded and set her on fire but we drove them off with our guns extinguished the fire and saved the cargo this was in the fall of 1777 the same year the English Sloop of War called the Otter and a fifty gun ship drove on shore a privation owned at Stoning and ton a schooner, her prizes, but they were prevented from boarding them, by the Militia, and were both saved; that a Sloop of one hundred and thirty tons with a full cargo of salt,rum, Cocoa, &c from Demerara, was driven on shore near Watch Point which was also defended and saved by the Militia, both Vessel and cargo; that an English Sixteen Gun Schooner in chase of an American Privation, ran on a Rock near Watch Point, and with our guns we prevented the Enemy from getting her off, and she was blown up by them; the Enemy had cruises along the shore, constantly by during the periods before mentioned, and frequently attempted to take the cattle from the adjoining Farms, which were generally prevented by our Guard. The said Capt Pendleton continued in command of said Company until the year 1780, and there was a Guard constantly stat- ioned at Watch Hill by the order and direction of Capt Pendleton, by detachments from his Company and others in Col.
